ordered_diagnoses: Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of the liver

s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal pain with liver dysfunction and a large cystic tumor
salient_findings: Elevated alkaline phosphatase and γ-glutamyl transferase
Large cystic tumor in the liver with solid components
key_facts: 65-year-old woman presented with right dorsal pain
Total bilirubin 1.3 mg/dL
Alkaline phosphatase 452 IU/L
γ-glutamyl transferase 167 IU/L
Indocyanine green plasma disappearance rate was 0.103
15-minute retention rate was 23.9%
Tests for hepatitis B and C viral markers were negative
Serum levels of α-fetoprotein, PIVKA-II, CEA, and CA19-9 were within normal limits
DUPAN-2 was 200 U/mL
CA125 was 321.8 U/mL
Neuron-specific enolase was 29.2 ng/mL
Abdominal CT revealed a well-defined, low-density, heterogeneous, multilocular cystic tumor
Tumor measured 16 cm in diameter
Tumor compressed the umbilical portion of the portal vein, the right portal vein, and the left hepatic vein
MRI showed mixed high and low signal intensity
PET–CT showed FDG uptake in the solid components of the cyst

shortlist: Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of the liver

shortlist.label: Mucinous cystadenocarcinoma of the liver
shortlist.why_kept: Multilocular cystic tumor with solid components and high CA125 levels

shortlist.label: Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of the liver
shortlist.why_kept: Large cystic tumor with solid components and high neuron-specific enolase levels

shortlist.label: Biliary cystadenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic tumor with septa and elevated DUPAN-2 levels

shortlist.label: Hepatic sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Solid components within the cystic tumor and FDG uptake on PET-CT

shortlist.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma with cystic degeneration
shortlist.why_kept: Liver dysfunction and large cystic tumor with solid components

raw.rationale: The patient's abdominal CT and MRI findings of a multilocular cystic tumor with septa and solid components, along with the presence of mucinous content and hemorrhage, are consistent with mucinous cystadenocarcinoma. The elevated CA125 level also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of the liver
rejected.why: While the tumor's solid components and heterogeneous appearance could suggest sarcoma, the presence of mucinous content and the tumor's cystic nature are more characteristic of mucinous cystadenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Biliary cystadenocarcinoma
rejected.why: Although biliary cystadenocarcinoma can present with similar imaging findings, the absence of specific biliary duct involvement or obstruction makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Hepatic sarcoma
rejected.why: The tumor's cystic and mucinous features are not typical of hepatic sarcoma, which usually presents as a solid mass.

rejected.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma with cystic degeneration
rejected.why: The tumor's multilocular cystic appearance and lack of significant liver function impairment or cirrhosis make hepatocellular carcinoma with cystic degeneration less likely.
